key_insight: Intensity normalisation changes MRI segmentation performance, but its effect is modest compared with the much larger drop caused by moving to a different dataset or scanner domain.
clinical_relevance: For knee MRI meniscus segmentation, choosing a robust normalisation method may help cross-site generalisation, but it is not enough on its own to ensure reliable real-world deployment.
method: Compared 7 intensity normalisation methods, including standard scaling, histogram-based approaches, and a GMM-based method.
Trained a 3D U-Net on the IWOAI 2019 dataset for meniscus segmentation.
Evaluated performance on internal and external test sets, including SKM-TEA, to test generalisability.
evidence_signal: Performance was similar within the training domain, but external testing showed significant differences between normalisation methods, with Z-score, Nyúl histogram matching, and CLAHE performing more robustly.
watch_item: The gains from normalisation were small relative to the overall domain shift, so deployment still needs additional robustness strategies beyond preprocessing alone.
paper_title: A Systematic Benchmark of Intensity Normalisation Methods for 3D Knee MRI Segmentation and Cross-Domain Generalisability
